hints.title: Concurrent Traversal on Sorted Arrays
hints.text: Both input arrays are strictly increasing. Traverse them concurrently from left to right.

hints.title: Path Accumulation Between Intersections
hints.text: Accumulate path sums sum1 and sum2 along each array until an element common to both arrays is reached.

hints.title: Optimal Decision at Junctions
hints.text: When a common element is encountered, take the maximum of sum1 and sum2, add the shared value, and reset both path sums to this new maximum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxSum(self, nums1: list[int], nums2: list[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        i, j = 0, 0
        sum1, sum2 = 0, 0
        n, m = len(nums1), len(nums2)
        while i < n and j < m:
            if nums1[i] < nums2[j]:
                sum1 += nums1[i]
                i += 1
            elif nums2[j] < nums1[i]:
                sum2 += nums2[j]
                j += 1
            else:
                common = max(sum1, sum2) + nums1[i]
                sum1 = sum2 = common
                i += 1
                j += 1
        while i < n:
            sum1 += nums1[i]
            i += 1
        while j < m:
            sum2 += nums2[j]
            j += 1
        return max(sum1, sum2) % MOD
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph search with cycle handling or exponential path exploration is unnecessary on sorted arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pointer linear merge operates in O(N + M) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate uses junction nodes to synchronize path sums greedily.
